justification: Apple's order is hardware dependent and includes panes this machine cannot fill; our sidebar lists only pages that have something real to show and never reorders
Settings is an application window opened from the launcher or the dock — the same contract as Command-comma
x-apple.systempreferences links addressed Apple's pane identifiers; ours resolve through our own registry so every address names a row that exists in this build
Three procedural backgrounds instead of an image picker because the shell paints its own wallpaper and has no image decode path for a desktop picture
Accent is a slot whose value comes from the theme and a high-contrast theme keeps its own; the contrast pair is asserted per theme
Four built-in themes rather than installable theme packages because a package format is a signed-artifact problem this release does not have
Light dark and automatic; auto follows the local clock and leaves a high-contrast theme alone because contrast was the choice the user made
macOS wallpapers are neither reproducible nor ours; the choice is the same three procedural fields named for what they look like
Slideshow spotlight and per-monitor backgrounds need an image decoder and a monitor model the shell does not have; cycling three procedural fields is a rotating colour rather than a feature
Dock magnification exists but size and position are one measured strip inside the layout pass; making them settings is a rework of that pass rather than a row
Reduced motion and high-contrast themes are real; there is no accessibility tree screen reader or zoom and the page says so instead of hiding them
The page reports framebuffer geometry and UI scale as measurements; changing the mode needs DRM which the crate's unsafe-code forbid rules out today
HDR needs a colour-managed scanout path; a linear framebuffer has no transfer function to describe so the setting could only lie
Night light needs a gamma ramp or colour transform matrix and the framebuffer path cannot reach either without unsafe code
One UI scale for the whole screen rather than per-output scale because there is exactly one output

The image has no PipeWire file interface and libpipewire is a dependency this tree refuses so the volume is set through WirePlumber own client wpctl by litric-sysd and read back with the same tool after every change: the panel shows a measured level or says the sound server has not answered

A notification centre with priority and do-not-disturb exists, and since 2026-10-26 it is fed by a queue on disk: what a program posts while the desktop is not running waits there and is taken at startup
Do not disturb suppresses banners while keeping history, the behaviour the corpus records; the flag lives in the shell and the queue deliberately has none, so the two cannot disagree
A focus session with an end time and per-application allow lists is still not implemented; the do-not-disturb switch it would drive now exists, and the queue records nothing while quiet
Battery and power facts are read from sysfs and reported as measurements; suspend and power profiles are requests the daemon cannot yet honour
About is the measured machine: version root filesystem processor memory and daemon facts all read rather than typed
The developer facts are the diagnostics page: the numbers a bug report needs without a registry editor

Wi-Fi needs NetworkManager integration and a secret-agent design; without both a list of networks would be a drawing. The quick-settings tile reaches the link switch and the re-read since 2026-10-26, and joining a named network is the daemon action that waits for a pane with somewhere to type an SSID and a passphrase

Bluetooth pairing needs BlueZ and an agent that answers pairing requests and neither exists in the tree; the quick-settings switch reaches the radio power since 2026-10-26 and a pairing pane still waits for that agent
Layouts come from the locale crate and the page lists the devices the kernel reports; per-layout options are not modelled
Locale time zone clock cycle first day keyboard and units are detected and shown; only the language is a setting while the rest are environment facts
The lock surface and the verifier are real through the daemon's AUTH VERIFY and unix_chkpwd; no booted image has been locked and unlocked yet so this row is not evidence of that
Changing a password needs the same privileged helper family as sign-in plus a policy for what happens to stored secrets; neither is designed
One account exists and there is no session manager to switch between more; a users page would list a single row
The capability broker resolves requests but there is no prompt surface and no persisted grant; a dialog with no store would ask on every call
One field searches applications windows actions settings pages and settings rows; there is no file or web index and results are ordered by text rather than by a learned ranker
An index has to be built and kept current; searching the filesystem on every keystroke is the behaviour this row replaces rather than implements

The panel keeps the tiles it can back and now carries three of them: a volume reading with quieter louder and mute, a network row with a link switch and a re-read over NET LINK and NET RECONFIGURE for the interface the kernel reports, and a Bluetooth switch that appears only where a radio an unblocked rfkill and a Bluetooth service all exist; every reading is measured (AUDIO LEVEL BT STATUS) rather than remembered and brightness stays absent because no provider can change a backlight on this image
backend: litric-sysd AUDIO LEVEL/BT STATUS/NET LINK/NET RECONFIGURE/BT POWER with litric-shell quick settings

justification: Grouping needs a window-group model in the window manager; the dock shows one entry per window and does not pretend to combine them
Halves and quarters are supported by the manager; the flyout the corpus records previews live window thumbnails and those do not exist

Tabs need a per-window model of several folders and the daemon has none: one request lists one folder, one trash listing serves the window. Both ends exist since 2026-10-26 (litric-filesd, and the window that drives it over LFP/1), so this is a window-state feature now, not a missing daemon
Clipboard history needs a store and a permission model for what may be read back; the shell keeps the selection only while it lives
Fluent's measured values inform the palette but are not copied: our tokens are our own numbers with a contrast gate per theme
The control states exist and the focus ring comes from a token; Fluent's exact motion timings and materials are not adopted
The same reason as the quick settings tiles: a control centre needs sliders over real providers and the panel that exists is not renamed to claim otherwise
Workspaces exist and snapping is halves and quarters; the additional-desktop behaviours in the corpus are a subset of that
The centre is fed by a queue on disk rather than by the compositor's memory, so what was raised while the desktop was down is still there; the queue holds text and the centre draws it
Banners have priority, a lifetime and a retire animation; the corpus records action buttons and inline replies on the toast, and those need an action model the queue does not carry
Do not disturb is a switch that suppresses banners and keeps history; a focus session with a start and end time is a separate row and is not implemented
Four priority levels exist and decide whether a banner appears and whether a note can expire; per-application badges and a priority editor need an application registry that this shell does not have
Windows' shell model -- a persistent dock, a top bar, quick settings and a mission control -- is the one this system borrows; the chrome itself is the V6 design, not a copy of Windows
The desktop is a composed surface: a wallpaper the shell paints, a grid of icons that are real hotspots, and a context menu with rows that act
Icons sit on the desktop's own grid and every one is a hotspot; arrange and sort are not separate commands because the grid is the placement
A right-click on the desktop opens a menu of rows, each a MenuAction the shell handles -- not a list that closes when clicked
Start's role is the launcher: an overlay with a search field, a list of results and arrow-key selection, opened from the mark or the dock button
The launcher lists the pinned applications the build ships, in the dock's own order, with the dock's icons
A recommended/recent section needs a store of what was opened and when; the launcher lists the installed set, and inventing recency from nothing would be a fake row
All applications and the search results are the same list: typing filters it, and the list is the full installed set rather than a subset
A user-sized start panel is a Windows preference about a panel this shell does not have; the launcher is sized by its content and the screen
Lock, sleep, shut down and restart are the power menu's four rows, each one an effect the shell acts on rather than a label
The launcher is keyboard-driven: arrows move the selection, Enter opens it, Escape closes the overlay, all through the same shortcut table as the rest
The taskbar's role is the dock: pinned applications, the running set, a search pill, and a trash tile, on one measured strip
Dock alignment is a measured strip centred on the screen; a top or left position would need a different layout for every panel that anchors to the bottom edge
The dock's size is a token, not a hidden constant: 46-px tiles in a 62-px strip, lifted 12 px, all measured from chrome.rs
Jump lists need per-application actions the applications do not declare; the dock offers open and close, which is what the app model can promise
Thumbnail previews need a per-window capture path the compositor does not expose; hovering a dock tile highlights it and does nothing else
An overflow menu exists for a bar that runs out of room; the dock's tiles are a fixed set and the strip is measured to hold them
The top bar's right side is the corner: network, audio, battery, power profile, notifications and the clock, each a hotspot that opens its panel
Badges, flashing and taskbar progress need an application-to-dock-channel protocol; the dock shows running state and nothing per-app beyond it
Agent monitoring is a Windows AI feature with no counterpart: this system ships no agent runtime for the dock to report
Typing in the launcher searches the registry's rows -- settings, applications and files the index knows -- through one entry point
Results carry their type: each row says whether it is a setting, an application or a file, so the same query reads as different kinds of answer
Web and Store suggestions would send what the user types to a provider by default; search is local, and nothing typed in the launcher leaves the machine
A widgets board is a second surface with its own feed and network policy; this shell has no widget host and no feed to put in it
The quick settings sheet is a stack of measured cards; POWER is a four-segment profile track and SYSTEM is four switches, each tile one hotspot
Network and Bluetooth each get a card with a switch and a measured state line, backed by the daemon's NET LINK and BT POWER actions
Media transport controls need a session bus and a player to talk to; the volume card controls the level and mutes, not a player
Notifications are a daemon feature: litric-notifyd queues them, so a notification raised while the shell is down is still there when it starts
Workspaces are pips in the top bar and a menu in it: each pip is a hotspot, and a window belongs to exactly one workspace
Switching is a real move of the visible set, driven by the workspace pips and the Win+1..9 shortcuts rather than a preview
A per-workspace wallpaper needs the compositor to hold one image per workspace; the wallpaper is one composed layer today
Alt+Tab opens the shell's own switcher over the running windows, held open while Alt is down, with the selection moving by key
Window management is litric-wm's: geometry, focus, stacking and snap, with the shell drawing the result and the title bar it composes
Snap groups are a remembered set of windows that move together; the window manager snaps one window at a time and does not own group membership
Snap assist needs the other windows offered as the snap candidates while a drag is in progress; the drag path offers zones, not candidates
Dragging to an edge publishes a snap zone and dropping in it snaps; maximize and restore are the title bar's own button and the same command
The shell draws each window's title bar and its caption buttons, sized from the design tokens, and every button is a hotspot with a command behind it
Restoring windows across displays needs a display list the framebuffer does not have; one screen is the model this shell composes for
Lock, sign-in and the session are one state machine in the shell: the lock covers the desktop and a verified password returns to it
The lock screen carries a clock, uptime, network and battery as glass pills reading the machine's facts, plus a Customize sheet
Sign-in is the account password, checked against the stored verifier by the auth helper; there is no PIN, Hello or passkey to choose from
User switching and a secure-attention screen need a session manager and more than one account; this build has one account and one session
Shut down, restart, sleep and lock are the power menu's rows, each one an effect the shell performs rather than a message
Update-and-restart flows need the updater's state in the shell; the update path is the image's, and the shell has no row for a pending update yet
There is no first-run experience yet: the image boots to the desktop with a pre-seeded account, so every OOBE page would be a page nothing leads to
Region and keyboard are chosen at build time and can be changed in Settings; the first-run step that would ask is part of the OOBE work, not built
Windows requires a network to finish setup; this system installs from an image and boots offline on purpose, so no page may require a link
A vendor account requirement is exactly what this system does not do: the account is local, created in the image, and never leaves the machine
Privacy pages belong to the OOBE that is not built; the settings they would set exist as real rows in the privacy page instead
Restoring from another machine's backup is a migration feature; there is no backup format to restore from and nothing that produces one
The capability broker answers allow and deny today; the prompt that would ask a person is the other half and is not drawn yet
A secure desktop for consent needs a separate surface the compositor can lock the input to; that switch is part of the prompt design
Administrator elevation has no counterpart: capabilities are declared by the portal and granted by policy, not raised per process
Camera, microphone and location prompts need those capabilities to exist first; the broker catalogs what the build actually has
File Explorer's role is the Files application, whose reads and writes go through litric-filesd rather than the shell touching the filesystem
Home is a list of places, and the folder view is the daemon's listing; there is no Gallery, because there is no media index to draw one from
The places pane lists the roots the daemon serves, each a hotspot that navigates rather than a label
The address is drawn as crumbs from the daemon's canonical path, so what is shown is what the daemon resolved rather than what was typed
The command bar's actions -- new folder, rename, delete, copy, move -- are the daemon's operations, and each one reports its result
Sorting is a listing parameter the daemon applies; the view switches between list and grid over the same rows
Selection is the application's own: a row is selected by click, and the commands act on the selection and say so when it is empty
A details or preview pane needs metadata the daemon does not report and a decoder for images; the row already carries name, size and time
Search inside a folder needs an index or a walk with a budget; the daemon lists a directory and does not yet filter recursively
Copy and move are daemon operations; the shell shows the result the daemon reports, and a failure is shown as a failure
The daemon refuses to overwrite: a conflicting destination is an error the application shows, rather than a silent replacement
Rename is a daemon operation on one segment, validated by the path rules before it is applied; voice typing is not part of it
Delete moves to Trash through the daemon, and the Trash window restores or purges with a confirmation before a permanent delete
The context menu is one menu component with rows from MenuAction, so a modern and a legacy menu do not exist as separate code paths
Drag and drop between panes needs a drag payload and a drop target protocol; the commands move files without a drag
Archive extraction and creation are the files crate's zip and tar readers and writers, not a shell feature
AI actions would send file contents to a model; this system ships no such service and the Files application never reads a file's bytes to answer a query
A properties dialog needs metadata the daemon does not report yet; the row already shows the size and modified time it does report
The dialogs the shell draws -- a dangerous delete, a confirmation -- are one dialog component with a kind, whose buttons are real decisions
An open/save dialog needs a picker over the files daemon and a contract for handing the chosen path back; the Files application is not a picker yet
There is no print subsystem, so a print dialog would be a dialog with nothing behind it
A share sheet needs targets to share to; there is no share service, and inventing a sheet of dead buttons is the defect this ledger exists to prevent
A folder picker is the open dialog with directories only; it arrives with the picker over the files daemon
The system tools this build has are applications and panels with real behaviour: the terminal, the activity window, Defender and the environments list
A screenshot tool needs a capture path and a save target through the files daemon; the frame dump is a development tool, not a user command
An emoji and symbols panel needs a glyph index and an insertion path into the focused text field; the shell has text input, not a picker
A touch keyboard needs a touch input device and an on-screen key layout; input is keyboard and pointer today
Voice typing needs a speech model on the machine or a service off it; neither exists, and the second would send audio away by design
A run dialog needs a command launcher contract with the session; the terminal is the way commands are run, and it is a real application
Windows 10 and 7 interface differences are history for a system that never shipped either; the shell has one design and no legacy mode
Super with an arrow snaps the focused window to the half or quarter it names -- six actions in the shortcut table, each bound to a real key
